spots.name: Casbah of Algiers
spots.summary: The Casbah of Algiers, commonly referred to as the Casbah, corresponds to the old town or medina of Algiers, founded in 944 by the Zirids. It is a historic district that has been listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1992.

spots.name: Djamaa el Djazaïr

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Djamaa el Djazaïr, also known as the Great Mosque of Algiers, is a large mosque located in Mohammadia, in the Dar El Beïda District of Algiers, Algeria.

spots.name: Ketchaoua Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ketchaoua Mosque, also known as Djamaa Ketchaoua, is a mosque in the city of Algiers, the capital of Algeria. Completed in the 17th century, during Ottoman period, the mosque is located at the foot of the Casbah of Algiers, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is on the first of the Casbah's many steep stairways.

spots.name: Notre-Dame d'Afrique

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilique Notre Dame d'Afrique is a Catholic basilica in Algiers, Algeria. It is the origin of the modern Catholic devotion to Our Lady of Africa.

spots.name: Maqam Echahid
spots.summary: The Maqam Echahid is a concrete monument commemorating the Algerian War. The monument was opened on July 5, 1982, on the 20th anniversary of Algeria's independence. It is fashioned in the shape of three standing palm leaves, which shelter the "Eternal Flame" under it.

spots.name: Bardo National Museum

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Bardo National Museum of Prehistory and Ethnography, is a national museum located in Algiers, Algeria. It was originally a palace built by the Algerian admiral Raïs Hamidou in the late 18th century.

spots.name: Museum of Antiquities

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National Museum of Antiquities and Islamic Art is an art museum in Algiers, Algeria.
spots.wikipediaTitle: National Museum of Antiquities and Islamic Art

spots.name: Botanical Garden Hamma
spots.summary: The Botanical Garden Hamma is a 32-hectare (79-acre) botanical garden located in the Mohamed Belouizdad district of Algiers. It was established in 1832.

spots.name: Djamaa el Kebir

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Djamaa el Kebir or Great Mosque of Algiers, is a mosque located in the city of Algiers, Algeria. Built in 1097, it is one of the few remaining examples of Almoravid architecture.

spots.name: Palais des Rais

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palais des Rais, also known as Bastion 23, is a classified historical monument located in Algiers, Algeria. It is notable for its architecture and for being the last surviving quarter (houma) of the lower Casbah of Algiers, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

spots.name: Cathédrale du Sacré-Cœur d'Alger

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Cathédrale du Sacré-Cœur d'Alger is a Roman Catholic church located in Algiers, Algeria. Completed in 1956, it became the new cathedral in the capital after the Cathedral of Saint Philip of Algiers reconverted into a Muslim Ketchaoua Mosque.

spots.name: National Museum of Fine Arts of Algiers

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Fri, Sun

spots.summary: The National Museum of Fine Arts in Algiers is one of the largest art museums in Africa. Opened to the public since 5 May 1930, it is located in the Hamma district, next to the Hamma test garden.
spots.wikipediaTitle: National Museum of Fine Arts of Algiers

spots.name: Ben Farès Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ben Farès Mosque, also known as Djamaa Ben Farès and formerly as Djamâa Lihoud, is a mosque located on Place Randon in Algiers, the capital of Algeria. The mosque is located in the Casbah of Algiers, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

spots.name: Djamaa el Djedid

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Djamaʽa el Djedid, also rendered Djamaa al-Djedid, is a mosque in Algiers, the capital of Algeria.

spots.name: Ali Bitchin Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ali Bitchin Mosque is a Sunni mosque in Algiers, Algeria. It's named after Ali Bitchin, who ordered its construction in 1622 CE. It is situated inside the Casbah of Algiers, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, located at the crosspoint between Bab El Oued and the lower area of the Casbah.

spots.name: People's Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The People's Palace, formerly Palais d'été, is a public building in Algiers. It was first built in the State of Algiers era, then became the residence of the Governor of French Algeria, and was the seat of government during the first three years of Independent Algeria (1962-1965).

spots.name: Dar Aziza

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Dar Aziza is a 16th-century Moorish palace located in the Casbah of Algiers in Algeria. Today, it houses the National Agency of Archaeology and Protection of Historic Sites and Monuments.

spots.name: Dar Hassan Pacha

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Dar Hassan Pacha is an 18th-century palace located in the Casbah of Algiers, Algeria. It was built in 1791 and used to belong to Hassan III Pasha, who signed a treaty with the US September 5, 1795.

spots.name: Dar Mustapha Pacha
spots.summary: Dar Mustapha Pacha is a Moorish palace, located in the Casbah of Algiers, Algiers, Algeria. It houses the National Museum of Miniatures, Illumination and Calligraphy.

spots.name: Thaalibia Cemetery
spots.summary: Thaalibia Cemetery or Abd al-Rahman al-Tha'alibi Cemetery is a cemetery in the Casbah of Algiers in the commune of the Casbah of Algiers. The name "Thaalibia" is related to Abd al-Rahman al-Tha'alibi.

spots.name: Dey Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Palace of the Dey, also known as Algiers Castle, is an Ottoman era palace in the city of Algiers, Algeria. Completed in the 16th century, it is situated inside the Casbah of Algiers, and settled by successive deys of the city.

photo.author: Yves Jalabert from La Rochelle, France

spots.name: El Barani Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The El Berrani Mosque is a mosque in the city of Algiers, Algeria. The mosque is situated inside the Casbah of Algiers, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and is located at Bab Jadid Street, aligning with the entrance of Dar al-Sultan palace.

photo.author: Yves Jalabert from La Rochelle, France

spots.name: Safir Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Safir Mosque is a Sunni mosque in the city of Algiers, Algeria. The Moorish-style mosque was completed in 1534 CE and is located inside the medina quarter of the Casbah of Algiers, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

spots.name: Museum of Popular Arts and Traditions

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Museum of Popular Arts and Traditions is an art museum in Algiers, the capital of Algeria. The museum is located on Rue Socgemah in the Souk El-Djemaâ of the Basse-Casbah district and welcomes around 47,000 visitors every year. Its displays Algerian art, including rugs, jewelry, pottery and costumes.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Museum of Popular Arts and Traditions

spots.name: Djamaâ Sidi Ramdane

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Djamaâ Sidi Ramdane is a Sunni mosque and mausoleum in the city of Algiers, Algeria. Completed during the 11th century CE, the mosque is a part of the Casbah of Algiers, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

spots.name: Boulevard Mohamed-Khemisti
spots.summary: The Boulevard Mohamed-Khemisti, named after former foreign minister Mohamed Khemisti, is a major artery and public space in Algiers.

spots.name: Algerian National Theater Mahieddine Bachtarzi
spots.summary: The Théâtre National Algérien Mahieddine Bachtarzi, formerly known as the Algiers Opera House, is a historic building in Algiers, Algeria. It was built from 1850 to 1853. It was designed by architects Charles Frédéric Chassériau and Justin Ponsard in the Baroque Revival style.

spots.name: Larbi Ben M'Hidi Street
spots.summary: Larbi Ben M'Hidi Street, formerly known as Rue d'Isly, is a street in Algiers, Algeria.

spots.name: Bab Azoun
spots.summary: Algiers, officially Capital City of Algiers, is the capital and largest city of Algeria, located on the Mediterranean Sea in the north-central portion of the country. In 2025, an estimated 4.325 million people resided within the urban area.

spots.name: Mohamed Racim Art Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mohamed Racim Gallery is an Algerian visual arts art gallery in Algiers, named after painter and miniaturist Mohamed Racim.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Zioui Brothers Stadium
spots.summary: Zioui Brothers Stadium is a multi-use stadium in Hussein Dey, Algeria. It is currently used mostly for football matches and is the home ground of NA Hussein Dey. The stadium holds 5,000 people.
